A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Backslash/BackSlash research. All 12 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and references, support comparison. Neither supplied PDF contains an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original compression and accuracy experiments across models and tasks, training analyses, quantization/pruning tests, and regularization ablations in Sections 5.1–5.4.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 3–6 and the training and deployment analyses in Figures 2–8.

M1.justification: Algorithms 1–2 retain the same DGGR objective, dynamic shape estimation, soft gradient clipping, quantization, frequency-based value mapping, and entropy coding. Backslash becoming BackSlash is a naming edit.

E1.justification: Table 5 retains IMDB sentiment classification, Enron-Spam classification, 20 Newsgroups topic classification, SQuAD question answering, and WMT-19 translation. No datasets, tasks, or test scenarios are added or removed.

E2.justification: The comparisons retain normal training, fixed-length/exp-Golomb/Huffman coding, and the L0.5, L1, and L2 alternatives in Table 6. The RCT legend becoming BackSlash in Figures 7–8 identifies the same method.

E3.justification: The reported model sizes, classification and next-token accuracy metrics, Lagrange-multiplier settings, encoding quantization step, and quantization/pruning sweeps match. No evaluation protocol or experimental setting is revised.

E4.justification: Both retain the multiplier sensitivity and parameter-distribution analyses in Figures 2–6, quantization/pruning tests in Figures 7–8, and DGGR versus fixed-Lp ablation in Table 6. Their questions and evidence are unchanged.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or statistical significance tests. No uncertainty-reporting practice is introduced.

E6.justification: The numerical results and plotted trends match throughout. For example, Table 4 retains BERT's BackSlash EG length of 2.64 bits and accuracy of 92.59%; Table 6 retains DGGR's 1.37-bit EG length and 91.18% accuracy. Table 6 only relocates the accuracy column.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the generalized-Gaussian-to-DGGR derivation, shape-parameter estimation, and L1/L2 special-case relationships are unchanged. No mathematical assumptions, proofs, or corrections are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions and compression, accuracy-preservation, and pruning-robustness claims. The added Impact Statement restates training-integrated compression and deployment relevance without introducing a distinct scientific contribution.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning regularization, sparsity, pruning tolerance, and adaptive DGGR remain unchanged, as do the unresolved optimal multiplier and future hardware work. The Impact Statement adds general significance language without a new mechanism, limitation, or applicability boundary.

D1.justification: The algorithm descriptions, quantization/value-mapping instructions, and disclosed parameter settings are retained. v3 supplies no new implementation, hardware, training-time, or code/data-access information.

R1.justification: The cited works and substantive related-work discussion match. Both distinguish training-integrated rate-distortion optimization from post-training compression; the added Impact Statement reiterates that positioning.

P1.justification: v3 standardizes BackSlash and DeepSeek capitalization, makes limited wording edits, and adds an Impact Statement before the references. It also revises author-role/front-matter text and adds conference publication information. The main narrative and section organization remain intact.

P2.justification: Figures 7–8 replace 'RCT Model' with 'BackSlash Model'. Table 6 moves Accuracy from the final to the third column and expands the compression headers. Front matter and references reflow, while all figures, tables, and plotted results are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 provides small editorial cleanup through consistent labels and Table 6 formatting, plus an Impact Statement reiterating existing motivation. The method, mathematical argument, empirical evidence, qualifications, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. These limited presentation edits leave overall paper quality essentially unchanged.
